info.title: arbitr API
info.description:
Programmatic access to arbitr.

Use this API to create translation projects, upload documents, poll progress,
fetch deliverables, and manage credits from your own tools. Authenticate with
an API key generated in the arbitr UI under **Settings → API Keys**. All
routes are served under the `/v1` prefix, which is itself the API version
marker.

**Required header on every call:**

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `X-API-Key` | `abr_live_...` — from Settings → API Keys |

`X-API-Version: 1` may optionally be sent for belt-and-suspenders
validation; it is not required.

**Scopes:** each key is limited to the scopes granted when it was created
(e.g. `verify:submit`, `verify:read`). A call to a route the key isn't scoped
for returns `403 insufficient_scope`. Check a key's scopes with `GET /v1/me`.

**Rate limits:** per API key. Live keys (`abr_live_*` / `py_live_*`): **100**
requests/minute. Test/sandbox keys (`abr_test_*` / `py_test_*`): **30**
requests/minute. Both share a **20** requests/second burst cap. Every
response includes `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and
`X-RateLimit-Reset`. Exceeding the limit returns **429** with `Retry-After`
(seconds) and `error.code` = `rate_limited`.

**Idempotency:** optional `Idempotency-Key` is accepted only on
`POST /v1/projects` (create). Other POST routes do not honour it — sending
the header there has no effect.

**Language codes:** every language in a response is a **lowercase BCP-47
tag** (`en-us`, `fr-fr`, `pt-br`, `es-la`), one of the `bcp47` values returned
by `GET /v1/languages`. Send those tags. A request code is resolved to one of
those languages, so any case and `_` work (`fr-FR`, `pt_BR`), and a bare
language code names that language's default variety (`fr` is `fr-fr`).
Language names are not accepted. On `POST /v1/projects`, a code that doesn't
name exactly one supported language, such as a bare code that fits several
varieties when none is the default, is refused with `422`. A stored language
that `GET /v1/languages` doesn't list reads as `null`.

**Submit a project:** `POST /v1/projects` takes a source file, a
`source_language_code` (required), a `target_language_codes` array, plus a
`workflow` — an ordered list of stages. `AI_TRANSLATION` is the required base
(machine translation and automatic verification); layering on `TRANSLATION`
(requires `AI_TRANSLATION`) and `EDIT` (requires `TRANSLATION`) routes the
project through the corresponding human stages after the AI stage completes —
arbitr assigns and sequences everything downstream of `workflow` automatically.
`["AI_TRANSLATION"]` alone is a valid AI-only project. An optional `due_date`
(`YYYY-MM-DD`) is informational only — it never blocks or parks the project;
feasibility is reported back on the status endpoint.

**Poll a project:** `GET /v1/projects/{id}` is the single status endpoint.
Alongside `status`, it returns an `assessment` block (billable words,
`due_date_feasible`, and per-wallet credit sufficiency —
`credits.intelligence` always, plus `credits.trust` when the workflow
includes a human stage) and a `review` block describing where the project
sits in its human-stage lifecycle.

**Credit shortfall:** if a project's credits run out mid-flight — intelligence
credits for the AI stage, or trust credits for a human stage — its status
becomes `awaiting_payment`. Top up the org's balance and call
`POST /v1/projects/{id}/resumptions` (or
`POST /v1/projects/{id}/review/resumptions` when the hold is on the human
stage) to continue (`409` if the project isn't awaiting payment, `402` if
the balance is still short). The former `…/resume` and
`…/human-review/resume` paths have been removed and answer `410 Gone`;
use the two routes above.

**Deliverables:** list a completed project's files with
`GET /v1/projects/{id}/deliverables`; add `?format=zip` to get all of them
bundled as one ZIP instead of the JSON list. Fetch one deliverable with
`GET /v1/projects/{id}/deliverables/{deliverable_id}` — omit `Accept` (or
send `application/json` / `*/*`) for its metadata, or send `Accept:
application/octet-stream` to stream the file bytes directly instead.
The former `…/deliverables/zip` and `…/deliverables/{deliverable_id}/download`
paths have been removed and answer `410 Gone`; use the two routes above.

Losing a key: rotate it from the Settings page. The plaintext is shown only once.

**Retired routes:** the superseded aliases above, plus
`…/agent-selection`, answer `410 Gone`. Where a successor exists, the
error body names it. `agent-selection` has no drop-in replacement —
choose the workflow at `POST /v1/projects` instead.

**Deprecations:** a route being retired stays callable until its sunset date
and is marked `deprecated` below. While deprecated, every response carries
`Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers (RFC 9745 / RFC 8594) so client tooling
can warn before anything breaks. The minimum notice from announcement to
removal is 90 days. After sunset the route answers `410 Gone` with a pointer
to its replacement.

post.summary: Create a translation project with a source document
post.description:
Create a translation project from a multipart upload.

Multipart form: send one or more parts named ``file`` (repeated) along
with ``name``, ``target_language_codes`` (JSON-array string),
``source_language_code`` (BCP-47, required), ``workflow`` (JSON-array
string of workflow stages), and optional ``due_date`` and ``requester``
(JSON-encoded object naming the person the project is for). Caps: 200 MB total
across all files, max 100 files per submission; no per-file cap —
a single file may use the full budget. ``workflow`` and ``due_date``
are validated server-side.

When ``Idempotency-Key`` is provided, retries with the same key replay
the original response (24h TTL). A concurrent or unfinished first request
returns 409 idempotency_in_progress. A new create needs a new key.

With ``reference``, there is one project per reference in your
organisation, for as long as that project exists: a create whose reference
is already in use returns the existing project with 200 and creates
nothing. This is separate from ``Idempotency-Key``; you can send both.
With both, a retry with the same key replays the first response first (a
201 stays a 201); a new key whose reference is already in use gets the
200, and its retries replay that 200.

get.summary: List verification findings for a project
get.description: Return segment flags and agent findings for one project. Requires the `audit:read` scope. Walk `page.after` as `?after=` until `page.has_more` is false. `page.number` is always 1 — do not pass `?page=`. A page may contain fewer than `limit` items when a stored row fails validation; keep walking — valid rows are not dropped. Order is `segment_index` (per batch, so locales at the same index sit together), then flags before agent findings, then `id`. Group by `locale_code` on the client if you need per-locale lists. `severity`, `category`, and `status` (`open` or `resolved`) filter flags only — when any of those is set, agent findings are omitted. Stop when `page.has_more` is false, never on an empty `findings` array — a skipped window can still have more pages.

JSON metadata by default; the raw file bytes when the caller sends
``Accept: application/octet-stream``.

Missing ``Accept``, ``*/*``, or ``application/json`` (including when
JSON is listed first in a combined Accept) returns metadata. To stream
the file, send ``Accept: application/octet-stream`` as the first usable
type. The response ``Content-Type`` for bytes is the file's real type
(for example ``text/plain``), not necessarily ``application/octet-stream``.

post.description:
Translate up to 100 texts into up to 10 languages each, in one synchronous call: at most 30,000 characters in total per request. Send language codes listed by `GET /v1/languages`, in any case, with `-` or `_`; a bare code such as `fr` names that language's default variety, and one that fits several varieties when none is the default comes back `unsupported`. Results carry lowercase BCP-47 tags. The source language is detected when omitted. Your organization's glossaries apply.

Set `format` to say what kind of text you are sending. `text` (the default) is plain text. `html` is an HTML fragment: the tags come back as you sent them, and text inside an element marked `translate="no"` or `class="notranslate"` is left alone. `slack` is Slack mrkdwn: mentions, channels, `<!here>`, emoji, links and code come back as you sent them, and link labels are translated. Markup counts towards the characters charged.

Each text is charged 1 intelligence credit per 300 characters, rounded up, per target language. A text already in the target language, or in a variant of it (en-us and en-gb, pt-pt and pt-br, fr-fr and fr-ca), is returned unchanged and not charged; only Simplified and Traditional Chinese are converted. A text with nothing to translate (only emoji, numbers, punctuation, links or mentions) comes back `nothing_to_translate`, unchanged and not charged; in `html` and `slack`, markup doesn't count as something to translate. A text whose language can't be detected is `undetermined` and not charged. When the source or a target isn't a supported language, or the language pair can't be translated, that target comes back `unsupported` and is not charged; the other targets still translate. A code that isn't a language code at all, or a text naming one target language twice (`fr` and `fr-fr`), fails the request with 422 and `field_errors`. A text is charged once per `ref` and target language: retrying with the same `ref` is free. When the organization can't cover the call, nothing is translated and the 402 response says how many credits are needed. If translation fails, nothing is charged. If a request and its retry both fail, the charge from the first attempt stays; retry again with the same `ref` to get the translation at no extra charge. If billing is unavailable (502), the charge may already have been made: retry with the same `ref`, which is never charged twice for a target language. Reusing a `ref` for a different text returns 409.

Beta: requires the `text:translate` scope.

**Idempotency-Key:** not accepted here — only `POST /v1/projects` honours it.
